newsitem.title: INDIA: India budget seen helping Reliance Ind.
newsitem.headline: India budget seen helping Reliance Ind.

text.p: The budget proposals for fiscal 1997/98, running from April to March, will help India's largest private firm Reliance Industries Ltd, analysts said on Friday.

"The reduction in MAT (minimum alternate tax) from 12.9 percent to 10.5 percent (in this budget) will help Reliance," Manish Kumar, analyst at Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) investment research division said.
"That's true," said an analyst at a European brokerage.
"Besides, Reliance, being a pivotal stock will benefit as the entire market gets a boost from this budget," he said.

A reduction in excise duty on polyester filament yarn (PFY) to 34.5 percent from 46.0 percent, announced in Friday's budget, is expected to be passed on by manufacturers to consuming industries and would lead to increased demand, analysts said.
"This was expected," said another analyst. She said the cut in excise duty would help PFY users at a time when the demand was down.
Reliance is India's largest producer of polyester yarn.
